title: Private nested interfaces
answer: Yes. A member interface declared inside a class may be private, which limits its visibility to the enclosing class. This is useful for an implementation detail or internal strategy contract that outside callers should not name. A top-level interface cannot be private because top-level types may only use the permitted top-level access modifiers.
